title: Divisive attenuation based on noisy sensorimotor predictions accounts for excess variability in self-touch
authors: Nicola Valè; Ivan Tomić; Zahara Gironés; Daniel M Wolpert; Konstantina Kilteni; Paul M Bays
evidence_type: peer-reviewed primary computational model and new/previously published human force-matching experiments
population: Healthy adults across adult age range plus schizophrenia/control groups; no Tourette cohort. Study 1 includes 93 new participants added to 28 previously reported.

sample.denominator_caveat: Table pre/post-exclusion status and Study 2 allocation not fully explicit; no pooled analyzed denominator asserted.

exposure: Direct finger reproduction versus indirect slider/joystick reproduction; separate study manipulates active-to-passive gain 0.5, 1 and 2.
outcomes: Matching-force means, SD, skewness; hierarchical attenuation factor mean/SD; DIC and posterior predictive fit diagnostics.
followup: Laboratory task; no prospective clinical outcome or disease-modification follow-up.
negative_findings: Mean-matched direct/indirect variability slope BF10=1.1 in Study 3 controls. Gain-contrast 95% HDIs and between-group attenuation-factor SD differences include zero; not equivalence. Schizophrenia model separation ΔDIC=2.5 weak despite favored direction.
risk_of_bias: Restricted comparison of two normal-factor models, not exhaustive mechanism test
Indirect attenuation assumed absent; shared memory/comparison and calibration required
Study 4 imports Study 1 indirect population parameters
Reused cohorts, heterogeneous apparatus/age, modest schizophrenia/gain samples
No held-out clinical prediction or prospective Tourette validation
adverse_events: No treatment evaluated; no clinical safety inference.
funding_conflicts: ERC TICKLISHUMAN 101039152 and Wellcome Trust 106926 reported; authors declare no competing interests.
cohort_overlap: Study 1 extends Kilteni and Ehrsson 2020; Studies 2–4 reuse Wolpe 2016, Shergill 2005 and Bays/Wolpert 2008. Related preprint DOI 10.1101/2024.06.20.599826 is not independent replication.
claim_supported: Divisive predictive attenuation fits these tasks under stated assumptions; target-only matching conflates memory with attenuation; gain manipulation challenges simple active-force gating.
claim_not_supported: A universally pure biological measure, exclusion of all nonpredictive alternatives, Tourette causation, clinical biomarker validity or treatment benefit.
access: Full main author manuscript via Europe PMC, CC BY 4.0 verified. No participant data, appendix fitting or unlicensed source retention.
reviewer: AI-assisted primary-methods audit; independent verification recorded separately by integrating run
correction_retraction_check: Europe PMC core metadata has related preprint link only; exact DOI correction/retraction web search found no notice. Bounded check, not exhaustive.
next_verification_task: Primary published aggregate audit of indirect-task learning and repeat-session reliability; stop if only participant data/contact available.
